data.name: _cache_dir
data.value: Where Osprey keeps the files it builds once and reuses in later searches: each run's {0} (its spectra, faster to read than the data file) and, for a {2} library, the {5} it is converted to (e.g. hela{2}{5}). By default each goes beside the file it comes from, or under {4} or {1} when that folder is read-only. Give it to put them elsewhere, for example when the data and the library are on a read-only share, or to let several analyses share one cache. An HPC run ({3}) that writes to an {4} away from the data should give every node the same one.

data.name: _decoy_pairing_manifest
data.value: With {0} and a {1} library: the FDRBench pairing manifest (a 5-column TSV) that pairs each decoy, and each entrapment peptide, with its target. A {2} library carries its pairing in its own table and needs none.

data.name: _decoys_in_library
data.value: Search with the decoys the library holds instead of generating a reversed decoy for every target. A decoy is recognized by the library's own decoy table (in a {2}), by its Decoy column (in a {0}), or by a protein accession starting with one of {1}; the search stops with an error when none is recognized.

data.name: _demux
data.value: Demultiplex overlapping-window (staggered) DIA to its narrow bins before searching (default: {0})

data.name: _diagnostics
data.value: Write developer diagnostic dump files, for comparison with the Rust implementation

data.name: _experiment_fdr
data.value: The experiment-level FDR threshold (default: 0.01): a precursor is reported when its q-value across all the runs is at most this. {0} says which q-value.

data.name: _export_library
data.value: Write the library given by {0} to this path as a {1} and exit without searching. It is the file a search keeps in its cache for a {4} library (e.g. hela{4}{1}): the library as a search loads it, with its decoys and their pairing in its own table (with {2}, and {3} for a {4}), so it needs no manifest, searches back exactly as the original did, and Skyline can import it.

data.name: _fdr_level
data.value: Which experiment-level q-value {1} applies to: {0} (the default; each precursor's own), peptide (its peptide's, over all its charge states), or both (the larger of the two).

data.name: _fdrbench
data.value: Write an FDRBench-compatible input TSV to this path. The level is taken from {0} ({2}; {3} and {4} emit precursor-level). Includes every reported target, i.e. the peptides actually written to the output, regardless of q-value, with the raw SVM discriminant as '{1}', so FDRBench can compute true FDR via entrapment counting without truncation at Osprey's threshold.

data.name: _fdrbench_pass
data.value: With {0}: which FDR pass to emit. 2 (default) = the second-pass results written to the blib (the FDR of what Osprey reports). 1 = the full first-pass pool, before it is filtered for the second pass (every scored target, regardless of q), with first-pass q-values, matching the FDRBench input of the original Rust Osprey (the assumption the second-pass output rests on). {3} = emit both in one run, writing the {0} path with {1} / {2} stem suffixes.

data.name: _fdrbench_per_run
data.value: With {0}: emit one row per (precursor, run) using run-level q-values (adds a '{1}' column). Default is one row per precursor using experiment-level q-values.

data.name: _fragment_tolerance
data.value: The fragment m/z tolerance, in the unit {0} names (default: 10 ppm, or 0.5 m/z with {1} {2}).

data.name: _fragment_unit
data.value: The unit of {0}: ppm or mz (default: ppm, or mz with {1} {2}).

data.name: _help
data.value: Show this help message ({0})

data.name: _input
data.value: Mass spectrometry data files to search: mzML, or any format ProteoWizard reads, including vendor files (.raw, .d, .wiff, .lcd) where the vendor readers are installed

data.name: _input_list
data.value: File of input paths, one per line (# comments ignored). Bounded alternative to a long {0} list.

data.name: _install_cuda_runtime
data.value: Download the NVIDIA CUDA runtime from nuget.org (several GB; the size is logged first, and every package is checked against the hashes this build was tested with) into the {0} folder and exit, so that {1} can predict on the GPU. Needs nothing else on the command line.

data.name: _library
data.value: Spectral library to search: a {0} (as {4} and CarafeSharp write it, or one from Skyline or BiblioSpec), or, for comparing with DIA-NN, a library in the {1} format DIA-NN imports, such as Java Carafe writes for it. Without {2}, Osprey generates a reversed decoy for every target, and a library that holds decoys is refused. With {2}, the library's own decoys are used: a {0} pairs them from its own table, and a {1} marks them by its Decoy column or a decoy accession prefix and pairs them by {3} (an FDRBench pairing manifest) or by composition.

data.name: _log_file
data.value: Write all output to this file instead of the console

data.name: _memstamp
data.value: Prefix each output line with managed and private memory in MB (pair with {0} for perfviz)

data.name: _model_diagnostics
data.value: Write a self-contained interactive HTML report of the trained scoring model, FDR calibration, and single-peak multiple-ID co-assignment

data.name: _no_prefilter
data.value: Score every library precursor in each isolation window, not only those whose fragments first show a coelution signal. About 30% slower; for checking that the pre-filter loses no detections.

data.name: _output
data.value: The search result, for Skyline: a {0} that holds, for every precursor that passes FDR, the library spectrum it was searched with (the predicted one, with {1}), the retention time and peak boundaries of its best run, its experiment-wide precursor q-value and PEP and its peptide q-value, and, for every run it was detected in, that run's retention time, peak boundaries and q-value. The protein groups its peptides belong to are in it too, with their q-values.

data.name: _output_dir
data.value: Write the intermediate files here - each run's scores and calibration and the analysis-wide FDR files - overriding {0}. The output and its reports stay where {1} names.

data.name: _parallel_files
data.value: Input files run concurrently by each per-file stage (OUTER) that has no flag of its own below. Absent: one at a time (default). No value: auto from free RAM and cores. <N>: exactly N regardless of RAM/cores. Distinct from {0}. Worth setting only for high-resolution data on a server with more cores than one file's search can keep busy (a multi-socket, NUMA machine); on a workstation leave it unset and let {0} use the cores.

data.name: _parallel_files_caching
data.value: Files {1} caches concurrently, overriding {0} for that stage only, in the same forms (a full run caches inside scoring, at its count). A vendor decode runs on one thread, so this can exceed the scoring count; mzML parses still run one at a time.

data.name: _parallel_files_rescoring
data.value: Files re-scored concurrently ({1}, and the second-pass per-file phases), overriding {0} for that stage only, in the same forms.

data.name: _parallel_files_scoring
data.value: Files scored concurrently ({1}), overriding {0} for that stage only, in the same forms.

data.name: _perf_stats
data.value: Emit the machine-parseable {0} lines that scripts and performance tools read (off by default)

data.name: _protein_fdr
data.value: Protein-level FDR threshold (default: 0.01)

data.name: _reconciliation_compaction_fdr
data.value: Peptide q-value threshold for keeping first-pass peptides for cross-run reconciliation and the second pass (default: 0.01 = {0}; loosen e.g. to 0.05 to broaden the reconciliation pool)

data.name: _resolution
data.value: How spectra are scored: {0} (the default; Orbitrap, Astral and TOF instruments) bins them finely, uses the MS1 precursor features, and matches fragments and precursors within 10 ppm; {1} (ion traps such as Stellar) bins them coarsely, without MS1 features, and matches fragments within 0.5 m/z and precursors within 1.0 m/z. The resolution is not detected from the data: a search of unit-resolution data must give {1}.

data.name: _run_fdr
data.value: The run-level FDR threshold (default: 0.01). A reported precursor gets an identification in Skyline in each run where its q-value in that run is at most this, or in its best run when it is in none; the scoring model is also trained and tested at it.

data.name: _shared_peptides
data.value: How a peptide shared by several protein groups counts in protein inference: {0} (the default; toward every group it maps to), razor (toward only the group with the most unique peptides), or unique (toward none).

data.name: _task
data.value: HPC: run exactly one task (one node = one task). Omit for the full pipeline. {0} stages the {1} caches; {4} writes the {5} parquets, and on a COMPLETED run only the missing ones; {2} regenerates only the {3} report for a COMPLETED run, writing no other output. With {6}, {7}, {8} and {9} run the library build one phase at a time, and the four search stages search the library it predicts, or with {10} the tuning runs.

data.name: _threads
data.value: Per-file main-search threads (INNER; default: all cores), divided across the files a scoring or re-scoring stage runs concurrently ({0} or its per-stage forms)

data.name: _timestamp
data.value: Prefix each output line with {0}

data.name: _torch_runtimes
data.value: The folder of installed libtorch runtimes, where {0} installs the NVIDIA CUDA runtime and {1} looks for it, each runtime in a folder of its own (default: Osprey\torch under the user's local application data folder). Skyline passes its Tools folder, so one download serves its AlphaPeptDeep and Osprey; a cluster job names a shared folder.

data.name: _training_export
data.value: Write {0} per run: every target precursor at run q <= {1} with the observed intensities of its full b/y ladder and per-ion interference evidence (for training CarafeSharp). Adding it to a finished run writes only the exports and re-scores nothing.

data.name: _training_export_claimant_q
data.value: With {0}: the run q-value at which another target counts as a claimant of a shared fragment peak (default: {1})

data.name: _training_export_max_q
data.value: With {0}: the run precursor q-value a target must reach to be exported (default: {1})

data.name: _training_export_xics
data.value: With {0}: also write each precursor's per-ion XIC matrix over its final peak boundaries

data.name: _verbose
data.value: Show more detail (e.g. per-fold Percolator iterations) that is hidden by default

data.name: _version
data.value: Show version

data.name: _work_dir
data.value: Write the intermediate files and the caches here instead of beside each input, so the data folder can be read-only. {0} and {1} send one of the two elsewhere.

data.name: _fasta
data.value: Predict the spectral library from this protein FASTA with CarafeSharp's models and search it, in place of {0}. The library is written beside the output as {1} and can be given to {0} next time; its working files go in {2}. The options of the Library Digest and Library Prediction sections apply, and with {3} those of Library Tuning.

data.name: _precursors
data.value: With {0} and {1}: predict a spectral library for exactly the precursors of this tab-separated table (columns {2}, in alphabase's notation, as Skyline writes it for its Build Library) and write it beside the output as {3}, the TSV peptdeep writes. The pretrained models or {4} predict; the Library Prediction options apply, the Library Digest options and the entrapment do not. With {5} and {6}, the FASTA is the training library the tuning runs are searched against, the models are tuned on them first, and the tuned models predict the table; {0} is then not needed, and the Library Digest and Library Tuning options apply to the training library.

data.name: _model
data.value: With {0}: predict the library with this saved fine-tuned model ({1}, from CarafeSharp's training) instead of the pretrained models. With {2}, the tuning starts from it.

data.name: _device
data.value: With {0}: where the library is predicted, {1} (default: the GPU when this computer has an NVIDIA GPU that can use the CUDA runtime and the runtime is installed, see {4}, else the CPU), {2} (the GPU; a run that cannot use it fails before it starts, saying why) or {3}. The log names the device every library phase ran on.

data.name: _entrapment
data.value: With {0}: add an entrapment peptide to every target (or to this fraction of the targets, {1} to 1), shuffled from the target or, with {2}, drawn from a foreign proteome, each with a decoy of its own. For measuring the true FDR with FDRBench, whose pairing manifest is written as {3}.

data.name: _entrapment_fasta
data.value: With {0}: draw the entrapment peptides, matched in mass, from this foreign-species protein FASTA instead of shuffling the targets.

data.name: _training_input
data.value: With {0}: tune the models on these runs before the library is predicted. The runs are searched with a library predicted as it is without this option, their training exports tune the MS2 and RT models, and the library the output is searched with is predicted with the tuned models. A run need not be one of {1}: one that is not is searched for the tuning only and is absent from the output. The tuned model is saved beside the output as {2}, which {3} takes next time. The options of the Library Tuning section apply.

data.name: _training_search
data.value: With {0} and {1}: the stage {2} selects is a stage of the tuning runs' search, not the output's: it searches the {1} runs with the library {3} predicts, writes into {4}, and writes the training exports {5} reads. Give it to every node of that search and the same command line without it to the others. The same four tasks for any number of tuning runs, one included.

data.name: _training_input_list
data.value: With {3}: a file of {0} runs, one path per line (# comments ignored), as {1} is for {2}: a long list of runs on the command line can pass the Windows command-line limit and hides the other arguments.

data.name: _task_files
data.value: With {0}: print the files the task reads and writes for this command line, one per line as input or output, the task and the path, and exit without running it: what a node must be given and what it hands on.
